newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches Kosmos spy satellite.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches Kosmos spy satellite.

text.p: Russia's Military Space Forces launched their last satellite of 1996 on Friday, a spokesman said.
"We launched a Kosmos satellite at 9.44 am (0644 GMT) from the Plesetsk cosmodromme," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone from the space forces' headquarters in Moscow.
The spokesman said the satellite would be used "in the interests of the defence ministry" but gave no further details.

Russian media said in November that the country had been without photo reconnaissance satellites for nearly two months after the last operable one burned up on re-entry into the atmosphere on September 28.
But military officials denied the reports. One said: "it is impossible that a superpower such as Russia could be without such satellites". Russia sent a spy probe into orbit last week.
Russia has launched 10 military satellites this year, compared with 21 last year and 37 in 1994.
